done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (anything the app's date reader parses, such as last 30 days, explicit dates and date ranges, plus a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: An amount with the currency word before it, such as `Show Actual above rupees 2025`, is still classified as calendar year 2025. `AMOUNT_YEAR_PREFIX_PATTERN` recognizes `₹`, `Rs`, and `INR`, but not `rupee(s)`; the linked/comparison checks also fail because they receive a prefix ending in `rupees`. The provider path consequently replaces the inherited/model window with all of 2025. This is new evidence beyond the ruling preserving `Actual to/of 2025` and beyond the now-fixed comma-grouped amount case.
findings.title: Not done: an amount is never read as a year

findings.body: The period matrix still calls `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`, whose model, executor/warehouse, audit, dimensions, reports, and resolver are fakes. The frontend period-control tests likewise mock the API, and the registered package test commands contain no Playwright/browser flow through a running API and real database. Named-period precedence, inheritance/aggregation, amount protection, and edited-period reruns therefore remain proven only at mocked service/jsdom boundaries, not by the required end-to-end user flow. The successful close run executes those same registered tests and does not close this prior blocker.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
